title: Single-drug-single-dose packaging and packaging before a patient-specific prescription is received
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.08(2)(a), a pharmacy or pharmacist may utilize single-drug-single-dose packaging for solid oral dosage forms. Under 247 CMR 9.08(2)(b), if a pharmacy or pharmacist places a medication in a single-drug-single-dose package prior to the receipt of a patient specific prescription, the pharmacy and pharmacist shall properly label the package and utilize a bar-code scanning or similar technology to ensure proper identification of the pre-packaged medication at the time of dispensing.
exam_relevance: Tests that single-drug-single-dose packages may be prepared ahead of a patient-specific prescription, and that doing so brings two duties on both the pharmacy and the pharmacist: proper labeling of the package and bar-code scanning or similar technology at the time of dispensing.
common_confusions: Assuming a single-drug-single-dose package may be prepared only after a prescription arrives.
Relying on a visual check at dispensing for a medication packaged before the prescription was received.
